db28a4060fd9fccc: KUALA LUMPUR: Men's pair Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun went into the French Open final focused on fighting for every point. They came away with the biggest title of their partnership.
The world No. 11 battled back to beat compatriots and world No. 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani 13-21, 21-15, 21-7 at Arena Grand Paris on Sunday to claim their first Super 750 crown.
With the win, they take home US$70,300 (RM287,034.90) in prize money.

"We did not think about winning or losing because we were the underdogs. We just wanted to play our best and try to get every point," said Wei Chong in the post-match interview with Badminton World Federation.
That approach carried Wei Chong-Kai Wun through an opening-game setback before they turned the match around and swept through the decider.
It was their sixth World Tour title together and their first since winning the Malaysia Masters on May 25 last year, ending a 17-month wait.
Their previous titles came at the Syed Modi International in 2022, Taipei Open in 2022 and 2023, and the Indonesia Masters and Malaysia Masters last year.
The victory also ended Malaysia's 22-year wait for another French Open men's doubles title, following Gan Teik Chai-Koo Kien Keat's 2004 triumph.
For Wei Chong-Kai Wun, the success was all the more meaningful as they had set no specific targets for this run of tournaments while Wei Chong recovered from a knee injury.
Asked about the knee after the final, Wei Chong said it was "almost recovered".
Kai Wun acknowledged that consistency remained an area they needed to improve, but said keeping their focus on each match had helped them through the week.
"Our consistency is not so good. We just focused match by match, and I told my partner to give our best until the end. We did that today," said Kai Wun.
Having rediscovered their winning touch, Wei Chong hopes they can build on the momentum.
"We have been partners for more than five or six years. Now we are back, and I think we can keep the rhythm going," he said.
f0b7e5c7e48fbf89: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional will contest the Melaka election under the coalition's own logo, with its candidates to be announced on Oct 29.

PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the number of seats to be contested and the list of candidates had yet to be finalised.
"PN is scheduled to announce our candidates for the Melaka state election on Oct 29. However, the details have not been finalised," he told reporters after a PN emergency supreme council meeting.
Takiyuddin said PN had resumed operating as usual after the Kuala Lumpur High Court stayed all decisions by the Registrar of Societies against the coalition.
The High Court on Oct 22 stayed the Registrar of Societies' suspension and deregistration of Perikatan Nasional pending the outcome of its judicial review.
The Election Commission has fixed Oct 31 for nomination, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling in the 16th Melaka election, following the dissolution of the state assembly on Sept 23.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan won five and PN two.
Takiyuddin earlier said PN would ensure its candidates in Melaka did not clash with those fielded by Barisan Nasional.
e14cf7ce2e4be9d1: THE 2026 RinggitPlus Malaysian Financial Literacy Survey (RMFLS) makes for rather uncomfortable and troubling reading.
It finds almost a full quarter of Malaysians aged 25 to 44 postponing or altogether forgoing marriage or a first child due to financial constraints.
The figure jumps to 28.9 per cent for those aged 25 to 34.

This latest survey flies in the face of assumptions that younger Malaysians are simply losing interest in marriage or parenthood. Earlier findings cited by the National Population and Family Development Board showed that 90.9 per cent of single respondents intended to marry, while 91.1 per cent hoped to have children.
For growing numbers of younger Malaysians, then, economic pressures are making aspirations of marriage and family harder to realise.
A worryingly large number are finding it increasingly difficult to reconcile the search for financial security with the desire to start a family.

Government efforts to encourage marriage and parenthood will have limited impact if the underlying barriers — housing affordability, stagnant wages, job insecurity and exorbitant childcare costs — remain unaddressed.

Financial incentives may help, but they cannot substitute for sustained policies designed to improve household incomes, expand affordable childcare and give working parents greater flexibility in the workplace.
Employers can and should do more by offering family-friendly workplaces and by not penalising employees with child- caring responsibilities.
One way to ease financial pressures may be to encourage dual-income families.

However, we may be pursuing contradictory objectives, too, if, on the one hand, official policies encourage more women to join the workforce while the reality in the job market is that women of child-bearing age are among the last to be hired, all else being equal.

Would it not help if, for example, official policy gave both husbands and wives equal time off for child-bearing and child-caring? If the trend towards postponing or altogether forgoing marriage and child-bearing for financial reasons persists, the implications for the country may be grave.
It will inevitably lead to fewer and fewer babies being born and an acceleration of our already ageing population.

The bright spot in the RMFLS findings is that respondents take seriously their responsibility to support their parents and/or parents-in-law, with a majority of even those earning RM2,000 and below contributing monetarily to ageing parents.

This is another area where official policies may be tweaked, with the government stepping in to relieve younger Malaysians financially through assistance to older Malaysians who have meagre or no monthly pensions to depend on.

Younger Malaysians should not be put in a situation where they have to choose between financial stability and starting a family. Rather than lecturing them about family values, policy-makers need to create the conditions in which marriage and parenthood become financially viable choices.

d199aacb80d08a52: PALANGKARAYA: Indonesian conservation workers rescued an orangutan ensnared in rope and her baby on the island of Borneo where the critically endangered animals are at risk from boar traps and wildfires, an official said Sunday.

The female orangutan named Gadis, about 25 years old, and her son Garis, 10 months, were found snared in a suspected trap early Friday near a village in Central Kalimantan province on the Indonesian part of Borneo.

"Gadis was found with the ropes tied to her upper right arm and lower left arms, and the wounds were bad because the ropes had torn deep into her flesh," local conservation official Muriansyah told AFP by telephone on Sunday.
"It looked like the ropes were set up as a wild boar snare trap," added Muriansyah, who like many Indonesians has one name.
Both were receiving treatment at the Orangutan Foundation International clinic near the village of Pangkalan Bun.
Wild boar hunting using rope snares is legal and common in parts of Indonesia as a pest control measure to protect crops, but illegal inside protected forests or national parks.
Officials have repeatedly cautioned that careless placement of snares near wildlife areas could instead trap endangered sun bears or orangutans.
Dozens of orangutans have also been rescued in recent weeks from rampant wildfires burning across Indonesia that have cloaked the Southeast Asian region in a toxic haze.
Two more were released in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Saturday after being rescued from an oil palm plantation.
Orangutans are critically endangered and only about 120,000 remain in the wild in Borneo and Sumatra – about half the number from a century ago, according to conservation group WWF.
Last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature said fires were burning in habitats containing 52 percent of Borneo's orangutan population.

9b6a06b8e7bfcb4f: AN Emirati official with Palestinian roots, Lana Nusseibeh has emerged as a late frontrunner in the race to lead the United Nations, campaigning on a reformist agenda and vowing to work for peace.

Since her official nomination last Wednesday, she has already garnered the backing of Gulf states but also faced scrutiny over her country's normalisation with Israel and Abu Dhabi's alleged role in Sudan's war.

If she succeeds, she would be the first woman and the second Arab to snatch the job in what would be a tour de force for the United Arab Emirates, a Middle East power that was under Iranian attack earlier this year.
In a campaign video, she vows if elected to "bring greater urgency to the work for peace" and "defend human rights", speaking in perfect English with a slight British accent.
The long-haired brunette, 48, sporting a red suit, projects the image of a modern Arab woman, one that her country has long sought to portray.
"Lana Nusseibeh has a thick CV," said Emirati political science academic Abdulkhaleq Abdulla. "She brings in the best of the UAE's diplomacy."
She stepped down from her post as state minister at the foreign ministry and as envoy to the UN and European Union to campaign for the top UN job.
A seasoned diplomat, she has also served as the UAE's permanent representative to the UN, from 2013 to 2024, the first woman to hold the post.
Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under a US-backed "Board of Peace", said Nusseibeh "does not give up when the room gets difficult".
"She is relentless, but never in a way that overwhelms people," he said.
Nusseibeh comes from a prominent Palestinian family of statesmen, uprooted by the creation of Israel in 1948.
Her family traditionally held the keys to the Church of the Holy Sepulcher in the walled Old City of Jerusalem.
Yet she has defended the Abraham Accords, under which the UAE normalised ties with Israel in 2020, drawing criticism from pro-Palestinian activists and commentators on social media.

Her grandfather was defence minister in Jordan in the 1950s and one of the first Palestinians to be in contact with the Israelis, while her father Zaki Nusseibeh was an adviser and interpreter to the UAE's late founding president Sheikh Zayed.
He currently serves as cultural adviser to the UAE president and was also a state minister.
Nusseibeh has two sons. She holds two Master's degrees, including one in Israeli and Jewish diaspora studies from the University of London.

Nusseibeh's nomination has sparked some backlash over her country's involvement in the Sudan war, where the UAE is accused of backing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) — accusations it denies.
Since April 2023, Sudan has been engulfed in a war between the army and the RSF, triggering what the UN has described as one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
"There is no candidate that is short of criticism... We'll just have to deal with it, especially the Sudan file," said Abdulla.

"The UAE has already stated time and again that all of these are media allegations, and we have already made it clear that... we deny all of them, and we do not send any arms or finance the RSF," he added.
It is tradition that the UN's top job rotates between different regions.

Under that premise, the role should go to a candidate from Latin America this time. But United States ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz recently said the focus should be on picking the "best candidate" instead of the region or gender.
In the latest informal straw poll held recently to gauge which candidates have a shot of becoming the next UN secretary general, every contender received an effective veto.

Five of the 15 members of the UN Security Council wield veto power and can shut down any candidate unacceptable to them, which happened last Friday when all seven candidates received at least two vetoes.

4b22ee1f7844c295: Being Mozambican is a matter of belonging — regardless of one’s origin, appearance, or surname
Originally published on Global Voices
Indians in Mozambique celebrating the Hindu festival of Navratri. Image by Kash_if via Flickr. CC BY 2.0.

In Mozambique, the word monhé has a much deeper history than its everyday use might suggest. Depending on who says it and the context, it can simply be a reference to the population of Indian origin, an identity marker, or a prejudiced remark. But behind the word there is a history of migration, trade, colonialism, independence, displacement, and, above all, belonging.

The question of who is Mozambican gets particularly interesting when we look at the communities of Indian origin, who have lived in the country for several generations. Are they Mozambicans? Indians? Foreigners? Or, in some cases, stateless persons? The answer cannot be found in appearance, surname, religion, or family origin alone. It is found in the country’s history and, particularly, in its nationality law.
A presence older than modern borders

The presence of people originating from the Indian subcontinent in the lands we now call Mozambique predates the country’s independence and, in many instances, predates the demarcation of the current political borders. The Indian Ocean’s trade networks connected the East African coast to South Asia long before 1975, the year Mozambique gained its independence. Over time, merchants, families, and whole communities settled in different parts of the country.

During the Portuguese colonial period, this took place within a political structure that gave people nationalities and legal statuses according to the rules of the empire. As such, “being of Indian origin” never meant automatically “being an Indian citizen.” A person can have Indian ancestry and at the same time hold Portuguese, Indian, Pakistani, or any other nationality, which could leave people in a complex bureaucratic situation. This distinction became especially important when the empire came to an end.
1975: When the question “Whose country is this?” took on a new meaning

Mozambique’s independence, made official on June 25th, 1975, did not just mean a transfer of political power. It also implied the need to define who would legally receive the new state, which was known as the New State. The Nationality Law of 1975 was key to answering that question. Among its provisions were rules that recognized as Mozambicans certain people born in the territory and resident in Mozambique at the time of independence, as well as other criteria related to birth, family links, and residence. The legislation would thus transform a heterogeneous imperial population into a national political community.

For many families of Indian origin who lived in Mozambique for decades or generations, this transformation would mean a fundamental change: no longer being legally associated with a colonial power or a foreign nationality and becoming part of the new Mozambican nation. But the experience of this transition was not the same for everybody.
When identity doesn’t fit neatly into a passport

Decolonization created situations where identity, origin, and nationality did not match. Imagine a family history across three generations: the grandparents born in India, the parents born in Mozambique during the colonial period, and the children born after independence. Which nationality should each generation have? The answer may depend on specific legal circumstances: place of birth, the parents’ nationality, residence in Mozambique at its independence, existing documentation, and any decisions to opt for or relinquish nationality.

Here, the issue of statelessness arises. A stateless person is somebody who is not considered a national by any state’s legislation. It is not an ambiguous cultural identity or feeling divided between two countries, but a legal status.

After decolonization, some people in former colonial territories, such as Angola and Mozambique, faced this problem: some were no longer recognized as nationals by the former colonial power without any other nationalities automatically being granted. This does not mean, though, that the whole Indian community in Mozambique became stateless. This generalization would be historically and legally incorrect.
“Monhé” is not a nationality

This may be where everyday language misleads us. The term “Monhé” may be used as an identity category, but it is not a legal category. Somebody called a monhé can be as Mozambican as anybody else born or naturalized in the country. They may have been born in Maputo, Nampula, Beira, or Quelimane, speak Portuguese or another Mozambican language, have had family in Mozambique for several generations, and never have lived in India. Your ancestry does not disqualify your citizenship.

Likewise, a person of Indian origin living in Mozambique can be a citizen of another country. And, in certain cases, they may have difficulties in proving or acquiring a nationality. As such, it is important to distinguish three concepts that are often confused: origin, nationality, and citizenship. A person’s origin may be Indian. Their identity can be simultaneously Mozambican and Indian. Nationality, though, is a legal relationship between an individual and a state.
A community across oceans
The history of so-called monhés in Mozambican identity also challenges an overly simplistic view of nationality.

Mozambique has always been a space where people cross paths. Africans, Arabs, Indians, Portuguese, and other peoples participated, at different moments, in the country’s social, economic, and cultural development. The Mozambican coast, in particular, cannot be understood without movements across the Indian Ocean.

This is why it may be inappropriate to think of the Indian diaspora as forever an “outsider” population. For many of these families, Mozambique is not simply the country where they live. It is the country where they were born, where their parents were born, where their ancestors are buried, and where they built their lives. India may be their family origin. Mozambique is, for many, a homeland.
The ongoing question

Around half a century after independence, the question of nationality continues to be more than a matter of just documents. It is a question of recognition. Who has the right to say “I am Mozambican”? Is it enough to have been born in the country? Have Mozambican parents? Have lived in the country for decades? Participate in society? Speak its languages? Share a collective memory? Or will some people continue to be seen as foreigners by many, despite legally being citizens? It is in this space between the law and general perception that many identities exist.

This evokes the concept of a “bridge” — Mozambique’s Indian-origin community historically finds itself between different spaces: Africa and Asia, family tradition and national identity, migratory memory and territorial belonging. But being between two shores does not necessarily mean not belonging to either. Sometimes it means belonging to both. And, for some, it means discovering that their family history crossed oceans long before modern passports decided which country a person belonged to.

The history of Mozambique’s monhés is thus also a history about the very meaning of being Mozambican. Not a story of people who simply “came from outside,” but a story of people who, over generations, helped build the country, while continuing to negotiate, within their families and wider society the fundamental question that follows all those who migrate: where, in the end, is home?
Written (Português) by Tirso Sitoe

a6ca87453dcb96c9: ROME: Inter Milan struck twice in stoppage time to complete a remarkable 2-1 comeback win over Fiorentina at San Siro on Sunday and return to the summit of Serie A.

Alex Jimenez's rocket strike had the struggling visitors heading for a shock win, but Marcus Thuram levelled in the 91st minute before winning a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute.

The result meant the Nerazzurri returned to first place, level with surprise fellow pace-setters Lazio on 22 points, while the Florence club's winless run stretched to four games to keep them in 18th spot.

Cristian Chivu's side had the better of the first half but could not find a way past David de Gea, who made a fingertip stop on a Pio Esposito header before showing quick reactions to parry Thuram's angled drive.
De Gea was alert again to parry a fierce Thuram strike over the bar early in the second half, but it was the visitors who struck first against the run of play after 65 minutes.
Former AC Milan player Alex Jimenez took debutant Inter goalkeeper Ivan Provedel by surprise with an audacious angled strike from distance that flew into the top corner.

Inter piled forward in search of an equaliser, with Carlos Augusto's glancing header coming off the top of the bar and De Gea denying substitute Petar Sucic, but they could not find a way through until the game was into added time.

Thuram guided a shot into the bottom corner to level the scores before winning a penalty when he was dragged down by Victor Valdepenas in the box, which Zielinski converted to complete a pulsating victory.
Later on Sunday, Atalanta host Frosinone and Genoa face Venezia before Juventus travel to Lecce and AC Milan go to Udinese.

0a83eef21ead6b7d: FOREIGN policy is rarely the deciding factor in United States midterm elections, when economic considerations usually drive voters' choices.
But this time, with Donald Trump's war against Iran and his sweeping tariff campaign pushing up costs for Americans, a president's approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue.

As the Nov 3 elections approach, there are growing signs that voters are drawing that connection directly, creating a major liability for Trump and his fellow Republicans and imperilling their control of Congress.
Those include a Reuters/Ipsos poll earlier this month showing some 78 per cent of Americans blame Trump's policies for rising prices that are outpacing their earnings.

Not since 2006, when president George W. Bush's Republicans lost both legislative chambers while he was mired in the unpopular Iraq war, has a US leader's handling of international events appeared so central to shaping the midterms outcome.

The political backlash for Trump could be even bigger, with opinion polls showing that voters feel the economic pain from high petrol prices and rising grocery bills in a way that they didn't two decades ago.
"The bottom line is people are experiencing the impact of Trump's war and other policies," said Christopher Preble, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.
"Now voters have a chance to register their discontent with how he's dealing with all this."

With Trump's approval ratings touching historic lows, he has left little doubt, despite his public claims to the contrary, that he sees the straight line voters are drawing between his foreign policy and their cost of living.
That has prompted some controversial policy moves in the run-up to the elections.

Chief among them was Trump's lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports aimed at bringing down fuel prices, a step his critics, including some fellow Republicans, say reinforces the impression that he is siding with Moscow in its war in Ukraine.

He has also pressed Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian refineries as he tries to shift the blame for high US petrol prices despite experts saying the surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the war he launched alongside Israel against Iran nearly eight months ago.

At the same time, he has promised not to order any new attack on Iran before the midterms, though the US and Israel are widely reported to be preparing for a possible major escalation after the elections.
Some Republican candidates have distanced themselves from Trump on matters ranging from the conflict in the Middle East to the trade war with Canada and his pressure campaign against Ukraine.
Midterm elections historically have been seen as a referendum on the performance of the incumbent in the White House.
And in one election after another in recent decades, the conventional wisdom has been that economic concerns — "it's the economy, stupid", as the Clinton-era adage goes — dominate voters' choices.

Opinion polls for this year's midterms, including the Reuters/Ipsos survey, show that while voters rank foreign policy low on their list of priorities, it is clear that most Americans see some of Trump's signature moves on the world stage, such as the Iran war and tariffs, feeding into their higher costs.

Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has shaken up the rules-based global order while his relations with allies have steadily worsened and the limits of US power have been increasingly exposed, say analysts.
Against this backdrop, Democrats are widely projected to gain control of the House of Representatives in the midterms, with the Senate also seen as increasingly in play.
But even with a shift in the balance of power on Nov 3, lawmakers will have a hard time reining in Trump's capacity to pursue foreign policy as he sees fit.

"For many presidents who feel politically constrained (at home), foreign policy is the area where they are able to act with relative freedom," said Jon Alterman of the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank in Washington.

Analysts say Trump's handling of adversaries such as Iran, Russia, China and even Cuba or his approach to allies across the globe could go either way — or he could simply lose interest and double down on his string of construction projects, such as the White House ballroom.

3209167a22cb313e: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court's stay on Perikatan Nasional's deregistration allows the coalition to carry on as a "fully functioning and operating political party", says its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
He was responding to a letter from Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali ahead of the coalition's supreme council meeting tonight.

Rejecting Azmin's reading of the court's grounds of judgment, Takiyuddin said the order deferred enforcement of the Registrar of Societies' suspension order and any further deregistration proceedings until PN's judicial review application is disposed of.
He said the appeal by the Registrar of Societies and the home minister against the stay did not change the coalition's status.

"As advised by PN's panel of lawyers, Rule 13 of the Rules of the Court of Appeal 1994 provides that an appeal does not operate as a stay of execution of the decision being appealed against unless the court so orders," he said in the letter, as reported by Free Malaysia Today.
Azmin had earlier today warned that the meeting could breach the Societies Act 1966, arguing the High Court had held that the stay did not automatically restore the coalition's status.
He said Bersatu believed that with a notice of appeal filed, "all parties should preserve the status quo of the RoS's decision until all levels of proceedings have been exhausted".
Takiyuddin countered that the court had made no order for the appeal to operate as a stay of execution.
He said Bersatu's representatives were still welcome at the meeting to voice their views and vote, as with previous invitations.
If they chose to stay away, he said, that would be the party's own decision and would be recorded as such.
Takiyuddin also responded to Azmin's demand that the coalition's leadership state its position on Bersatu's own supreme council meeting failing to meet quorum.
Azmin had said this was used as an excuse to bar Bersatu from the coalition's July meeting.
Takiyuddin said Perikatan Nasional invited Bersatu to its Sept 20 supreme council meeting after accepting the registrar's ruling that it could not intervene in Bersatu's internal dispute.

But he said "the same standard was not applied" to the coalition, whose own internal affairs, including who could attend its July 16 meeting, became the basis for the notice, suspension and deregistration orders following Bersatu's complaint.
He also disputed Azmin's claim that the registrar had affirmed Bersatu as a legitimate component party in a letter dated Aug 12, saying it had never been provided to the coalition.

"If such a letter exists, it was issued a day after Bersatu's complaint was received by the RoS on or around Aug 11, before any notice was issued to PN and before PN's explanation dated Aug 19 was considered," he said.
Takiyuddin gave Azmin three days to provide copies of the letter and Bersatu's complaint, including all attachments.

On Oct 22, High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad allowed PN's application for a stay pending its judicial review challenging the Registrar of Societies' action. Takiyuddin said then that the coalition would invite Bersatu to an upcoming meeting.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Takiyuddin for confirmation of the letter sent to Azmin.

4da01de58a150bf8: KUALA LUMPUR: An estimated crowd of over 10,000 guests gathered in Muar, Johor, this afternoon for the wedding reception of Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and popular actress Bella Astillah.

Conceived as a kenduri rakyat (people's feast), the grand affair drew well-wishers not only from the local community, but also from across Malaysia — including Perlis, Kedah, Terengganu, Kelantan, Sabah, and Sarawak — as well as neighbouring Singapore.
Although official proceedings were scheduled to begin at 1.30pm at the Yong Sheng Banquet Hall, eager crowds had started lining up as early as 6am.
By the time the newlyweds arrived, a massive, snaking queue had formed under the blazing sun.
Police officers and civil volunteer corps personnel were on hand to escort the couple safely into the venue as excited onlookers surged forward.
Addressing the crowd, Syed Saddiq thanked everyone for their overwhelming support.
"I asked for her (Bella's) permission to keep my speech brief because I want to spend as much time as possible with the people who have been waiting outside in the blazing heat for hours.
"We are deeply indebted to everyone who came — some travelled from Perlis, Kedah, and Terengganu, others flew in from Kuching, and some even drove up from Singapore.
"We apologise from the bottom of our hearts for any shortcomings.
"We never expected people to start queuing as early as 6am all the way until 2pm, so we will do our best to meet as many of you as possible," the Muar MP said.
The couple, affectionately known as BASS, turned heads in matching light blue traditional Malay outfits adorned with subtle gold lining, custom-designed by Rizman Ruzaini.

Rather than hosting a purely private affair, the couple designed the reception to share their joy directly with the public, securing over RM500,000 in sponsorships that were channelled back to the community.

"Thank you to everyone who made this mission a success, returning RM500,000 in the form of food, drinks, tens of thousands of kilogrammes of rice, coconut milk, and basic items for the people of Muar," Syed Saddiq shared on social media.

As part of the initiative, local brand Jasmine Food Corporation sponsored 1kg packs of rice and 200ml boxes of coconut milk as door gifts for the first 10,000 attendees. Laptops were also distributed in conjunction with the event.
To feed the massive turnout, at least 15 local food and beverage vendors set up stalls on site, serving up coffee, pizza, fried chicken, ayam gepuk, and ice cream.
To help ease traffic and transport, organisers provided guests with a special Grab discount code, BASS25.
Syed Saddiq, 33, and Bella, 31, officially tied the knot on Oct 10 during an akad nikah (solemnisation) ceremony on the 118th floor of Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur.
This was followed by a reception at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) on Oct 18.
Following the Muar reception, the newlyweds will host another kenduri rakyat in Bella's home state of Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on Oct 31 as a token of appreciation to their East Malaysian fans.

9dbbfb6894e72b07: PETALING JAYA: National mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing’s remarkable run at the French Open came to an end in the final today when they were outplayed by China’s world No 1 pair, Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping.
It was the second time that the Chinese pair had denied the Malaysians their first World Tour title after their encounter in the China Masters final last month.
Pang Ron-Pei Jing, who were playing in only their ninth tournament since pairing up in May, went down 10-21, 13-21 in 36 minutes at the Arena Grand Paris.
Yan Zhe-Dong Ping have now beaten them in all three encounters so far.

Despite their loss, Pang Ron-Pei Jing have had a superb run on the world tour, finishing as runners-up in the China Open last month, and as semi-finalists in the Denmark Open last week and the Macau Open in June.
Yesterday, they also became the first professional Malaysian mixed doubles pair to enter the French Open final in the tournament’s 117-year history.
311525577ba5a1a5: ROME: Inter Milan struck twice in stoppage time to complete a remarkable 2-1 comeback win over Fiorentina at San Siro on Sunday and return to the summit of Serie A.

Alex Jimenez's rocket strike had the struggling visitors heading for a shock win, but Marcus Thuram levelled in the 91st minute before winning a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute.

The result meant the Nerazzurri returned to first place, level with surprise fellow pace-setters Lazio on 22 points, while the Florence club's winless run stretched to four games to keep them in 18th spot.

Cristian Chivu's side had the better of the first half but could not find a way past David de Gea, who made a fingertip stop on a Pio Esposito header before showing quick reactions to parry Thuram's angled drive.
De Gea was alert again to parry a fierce Thuram strike over the bar early in the second half, but it was the visitors who struck first against the run of play after 65 minutes.
Former AC Milan player Alex Jimenez took debutant Inter goalkeeper Ivan Provedel by surprise with an audacious angled strike from distance that flew into the top corner.

Inter piled forward in search of an equaliser, with Carlos Augusto's glancing header coming off the top of the bar and De Gea denying substitute Petar Sucic, but they could not find a way through until the game was into added time.

Thuram guided a shot into the bottom corner to level the scores before winning a penalty when he was dragged down by Victor Valdepenas in the box, which Zielinski converted to complete a pulsating victory.
Later on Sunday, Atalanta host Frosinone and Genoa face Venezia before Juventus travel to Lecce and AC Milan go to Udinese.

MetMalaysia issues a thunderstorm warning when there are signs of thunderstorms with rainfall exceeding 20mm an hour that is occurring or expected to occur for more than an hour.
Thunderstorm warnings are short-term alerts valid for no more than six hours per issuance.

b2cc2fb9a9101a23: JERUSALEM: Israel's central bank has issued a rare rebuke of recent remarks from prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggesting that the country use cryptocurrency to help establish an "alternative economy" to withstand possible sanctions.

"Cryptocurrencies cannot be used as a way to bypass sanctions on Israel.

"What is right for Israel's economy is to preserve our economic relations with our main trading partners and focus on preventing sanctions and their negative impact on the economy," the Bank of Israel said in a statement on Saturday night.

ac3fdeb95dc3d712: PETALING JAYA: Perintah Mahkamah Tinggi yang menangguhkan pembatalan pendaftaran Perikatan Nasional (PN) membolehkan gabungan itu terus berfungsi dan beroperasi sepenuhnya sebagai sebuah parti politik, kata Setiausaha Agungnya Takiyuddin Hassan.

Mengulas surat yang dihantar Setiausaha Agung Bersatu Azmin Ali hari ini, Takiyuddin berkata beliau tidak bersetuju dengan tafsiran Azmin terhadap alasan penghakiman Mahkamah Tinggi berhubung pembatalan pendaftaran gabungan itu.

Beliau berkata, perintah mahkamah itu menangguhkan pelaksanaan perintah penggantungan dikeluarkan JPPM serta prosiding lanjut untuk membatalkan pendaftaran PN sementara menunggu pelupusan muktamad permohonan semakan kehakimannya.
Takiyuddin berkata, rayuan yang difailkan JPPM dan menteri dalam negeri terhadap perintah itu tidak menjejaskan status PN.

“Seperti yang dinasihatkan panel peguam PN, Kaedah 13 Kaedah-Kaedah Mahkamah Rayuan 1994 memperuntukkan bahawa sesuatu rayuan tidak berfungsi sebagai penangguhan pelaksanaan keputusan yang dirayu melainkan jika diperintahkan oleh mahkamah,” katanya dalam surat kepada Azmin yang dilihat FMT.

Terdahulu, Azmin berkata mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi PN yang diadakan malam ini mungkin melanggar Akta Pertubuhan 1966, memandangkan Mahkamah Tinggi memutuskan bahawa penangguhan itu tidak bermaksud status gabungan berkenaan dipulihkan secara automatik.

Beliau menyatakan bahawa JPPM dan menteri dalam negeri telah memfailkan rayuan terhadap perintah penangguhan itu. Katanya, Bersatu berpendirian bahawa memandangkan notis rayuan telah difailkan, 'semua pihak hendaklah mengekalkan status quo keputusan JPPM sehingga semua peringkat prosiding selesai'.
Bagaimanapun, Takiyuddin berkata mahkamah tidak memerintahkan supaya notis rayuan yang difailkan JPPM dan menteri dalam negeri itu berfungsi sebagai penangguhan pelaksanaan keputusan.

Beliau berkata, wakil Bersatu masih dialu-alukan menghadiri mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi PN untuk menyuarakan pandangan dan mengundi, selaras dengan jemputan yang diberikan kepada Bersatu sebelum ini bagi menghadiri mesyuarat PN.
Katanya, sekiranya wakil Bersatu memilih untuk tidak hadir, keputusan itu merupakan pilihan parti berkenaan sendiri dan akan direkodkan sedemikian.
Layanan berbeza dikenakan terhadap PN dan Bersatu

Takiyuddin turut menjawab tuntutan Azmin supaya kepimpinan PN menyatakan pendirian berhubung isu mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi Bersatu sendiri yang gagal memenuhi kuorum ditetapkan. Azmin mendakwa kepimpinan PN menggunakan perkara itu sebagai alasan untuk menafikan hak Bersatu menghadiri mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi PN pada Julai lalu.

Beliau berkata, memandangkan PN menerima keputusan JPPM bahawa pendaftar itu tidak boleh campur tangan dalam pertikaian berhubung Majlis Tertinggi Bersatu kerana ia merupakan urusan dalaman parti, PN telah menjemput Bersatu menghadiri mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi pada 20 September.

Katanya, 'standard yang sama tidak dikenakan' terhadap PN apabila urusan dalaman gabungan itu, termasuk persoalan pihak yang berhak menghadiri mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi pada 16 Julai, dijadikan asas kepada notis, perintah penggantungan dan perintah pembatalan pendaftaran susulan aduan Bersatu.

Takiyuddin turut mempertikaikan dakwaan Azmin bahawa JPPM mengesahkan status Bersatu sebagai parti komponen PN yang sah menerusi surat bertarikh 12 Ogos, dengan berkata surat itu tidak pernah diserahkan kepada PN.

“Jika surat sedemikian wujud, ia dikeluarkan sehari selepas aduan Bersatu diterima JPPM pada atau sekitar 11 Ogos, sebelum sebarang notis dikeluarkan kepada PN dan sebelum penjelasan PN bertarikh 19 Ogos dipertimbangkan,” katanya.
Beliau meminta Azmin memberikan salinan surat itu serta aduan yang dikemukakan Bersatu kepada JPPM pada atau sekitar 11 Ogos, termasuk semua lampiran, kepada PN dalam tempoh tiga hari.

JPPM menggantung PN pada 23 September sebelum membatalkan pendaftaran gabungan itu pada Selasa lalu susulan aduan Bersatu terhadap kepimpinan gabungan berkenaan. Mahkamah Tinggi menggantung pelaksanaan keputusan itu dua hari kemudian.

65739c79738ee8a9: PETALING JAYA: The High Court’s order on Thursday staying the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional allows it to continue as a “fully functioning and operating political party”, says PN secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan.

Responding to a letter sent by Bersatu secretary-general Azmin Ali earlier today, Takiyuddin said he disagreed with Azmin’s interpretation of the High Court’s grounds of judgment on the coalition’s deregistration.

He said the court order deferred the enforcement of the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) suspension order and further proceedings to deregister PN, pending the final disposal of its application for judicial review.
The appeal filed by the RoS and the home minister against the stay of deregistration did not affect its status, Takiyuddin said.

“As advised by PN’s panel of lawyers, Rule 13 of the Rules of the Court of Appeal 1994 provides that an appeal does not operate as a stay of execution of the decision being appealed against unless the court so orders,” he said in a letter to Azmin sighted by FMT.

Earlier today, Azmin said the PN supreme council meeting being held tonight could be in breach of the Societies Act 1966, as the High Court had held that the stay did not amount to an automatic restoration of the coalition’s status.

He pointed out that the RoS and the home minister had appealed against the stay, and said Bersatu believed that since a notice of appeal had been filed, “all parties should preserve the status quo of the RoS’s decision until all levels of proceedings have been exhausted”.
However, Takiyuddin said the court had not ordered the notice of appeal filed by the RoS and the home minister to act as a stay of execution.

He said Bersatu's representatives remained welcome to attend tonight’s PN supreme council meeting, where they could express their views and vote, consistent with previous invitations extended to Bersatu for PN meetings.
If Bersatu’s representatives chose not to attend, he said, that would be the party’s own decision and would be recorded as such.
'Different standards applied to PN and Bersatu'

Takiyuddin also responded to Azmin’s demand that the PN leadership state their position on the issue of Bersatu’s own supreme council meeting failing to meet the required quorum, which Azmin said the PN leadership had used as an excuse to deny Bersatu the right to attend the last PN supreme council meeting in July.

He said that since PN had accepted the RoS’s ruling that the registrar could not interfere in the dispute over Bersatu’s supreme council because it was an internal matter, PN had invited Bersatu to its supreme council meeting on Sept 20.

He said “the same standard was not applied” to PN, as its internal affairs, including the question of who had the right to attend its July 16 supreme council meeting, were made the basis of the notice, suspension order, and deregistration order following Bersatu’s complaint.
Takiyuddin also disputed Azmin’s claim that the RoS had affirmed Bersatu’s status as a legitimate component party of PN in a letter dated Aug 12, saying the letter had never been provided to PN.

“If such a letter exists, it was issued a day after Bersatu’s complaint was received by the RoS on or around Aug 11, before any notice was issued to PN and before PN’s explanation dated Aug 19 was considered,” he said.
He asked Azmin to provide PN with a copy of the letter and the complaint lodged by Bersatu with the RoS on or around Aug 11, including all attachments, within three days.
The RoS suspended PN on Sept 23 before deregistering it last Tuesday following a complaint by Bersatu against the coalition’s leadership. The High Court stayed the deregistration two days later.

16f90ee08926f200: AMMAN: Jordan Football Association president Prince Ali bin Hussein accused Fifa president Gianni Infantino on Sunday of hijacking the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Congress for political purposes ahead of his reelection bid for a fourth term.
At the AFC's extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, its president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa endorsed Infantino's bid for reelection as Fifa president.

Months after the confederation accused Infantino of a "fundamental breach of trust" over the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, Sheikh Salman told the congress that Asia was now united behind Infantino.
However, Prince Ali, who has been a vocal critic of Fifa's leadership, painted a starkly different picture of events in Tokyo.

"Having come back from Tokyo where the AFC Congress took place, the first two days were about football, which we all serve. The last day was pure politics at the behest of Gianni Infantino," Prince Ali wrote on X.
"There were reports that Asia has a united position when it comes to electing the next Fifa president. In fact, nobody was allowed to speak, question, debate, or talk with the media.
"Lack of transparency leads to lack of accountability. No amount of coercion, threats or bribes should be allowed," he said.
Prince Ali did not elaborate on his statement. Reuters has contacted Fifa and AFC for comment.
Infantino also addressed the AFC Congress, giving Sheikh Salman his backing for another term.
In August, Prince Ali launched a public attack on Infantino, accusing him of "blackmail" and saying Fifa had offered to help solve the kingdom's problems in exchange for his endorsement.
Two days later, Prince Ali confirmed Jordan's players and staff had received outstanding reward money for their participation in the 2025 Arab Cup.
The association had been waiting since December for prize money for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

On Saturday, Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FFE proposal, pointing to what he described as overwhelming support from member associations around the globe.
The Swiss-Italian administrator's reelection prospects were strengthened significantly after the AFC endorsement, leaving Europe increasingly isolated and exposing the lack of a challenger.

5ffbda805adf9b6d: SEOUL, Oct 25 — The number of accidents and incidents involving South Korean nationals in 10 countries under Seoul’s travel advisories rose nearly 50 per cent in 2025 from the previous year, Yonhap News Agency reported, citing data released on Sunday.

In the 10 countries for which Seoul issued travel advisories most frequently over the past five years, cases involving South Korean nationals totalled 4,016 in 2025, up 48.3 per cent from 2024, according to data from the foreign ministry and the National Police Agency submitted to Representative Kim Joon-hwan of the ruling Democratic Party.
The countries are Russia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cambodia, Thailand, China, El Salvador, Mexico, Lebanon, Iran and Laos.
Cases of losing contact saw the sharpest rise, increasing to 617 in 2025 from 248 the previous year, the data showed.
Kidnapping and confinement cases more than doubled to 553 last year from 246 in 2024.
Cases of suspected missing persons jumped nearly fivefold to 188 in 2025.
By country, accidents and incidents involving South Koreans increased the most in China, with cases rising to 1,580 from 1,133 the previous year.
In Cambodia, such cases rose from 569 to 917 last year, accounting for 43.5 per cent of the total year on year increase across the 10 countries, the latest findings showed.

A police unit in Cambodia dedicated exclusively to crimes involving South Koreans, known as the Korea Desk, was launched last November to tackle rising crimes targeting South Koreans, including online scams.
Eight South Koreans have since been rescued and 107 arrested in a joint crackdown on scam operations in Cambodia. — Bernama-Yonhap
df70790ae9e76c4e: SEOUL, Oct 25 — The latest instalment of the Call of Duty video game franchise, featuring a full-scale North Korean invasion of South Korea, has topped sales charts in the would-be target, even as real-life border tensions are ratcheting higher.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, the latest edition of the globally popular franchise, is set against a backdrop of tensions between the United States and Russia.
Its Friday release comes on the heels of an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean soldiers, further straining ties on the peninsula.

The game follows several parallel storylines: a squad of young American and South Korean soldiers fighting for survival, a former serviceman driven by revenge, and a power struggle surrounding a new North Korean leader — a character players can also take on.
The new edition has generated considerable interest in South Korea, where able-bodied men are required to serve between 18 and 21 months in the military, depending on the branch.
The title has topped both the global and South Korean sales charts on Steam, one of the world’s largest digital distribution platforms for PC games.
The campaign begins with a surprise invasion of South Korea by North Korean forces, who deploy paratroopers and infiltrate through an underground tunnel to catch South Korean and US troops off guard.
In reality, the US stations about 28,000 troops in South Korea to help deter the nuclear-armed North.
Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war because the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

Reactions among South Korean gamers have been largely positive, with some posting hashtags featuring a Korean slogan meaning “exterminate communism” on social media and others saying they were considering upgrading their computers or buying new consoles to play the title.
“I cried so much playing the game to a point I almost got dehydrated. It reminds me so much of my grandfather, who fought in the Korean War,” a Threads user with the handle b_yeol_t said.
Another user, posting under the handle ireozima_zebal, described the experience as “horrifying” because of its implications for a potential conflict on the Korean peninsula.

“This is what would unfold if the North launched an invasion, with the border province of Gangwon overwhelmed within an hour and our defence line pushed back right on the edge of Seoul,” the user said.
But the game has also drawn criticism for turning the fraught history between North and South Korea into entertainment.

The title raises the “question of whether it is appropriate... to present the tragedy of the Korean War and the current antagonism between South and North as something to be consumed for entertainment”, Kim Sung-jae, chairman of the Kim Dae Jung Peace Center, wrote in the Hankyoreh newspaper last month.
On Saturday, North Korean state media said leader Kim Jong Un had urged his military to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang last week. — AFP
057c2882eed7c2e0: PARIS, Oct 25 — AFP has deployed reporters, photographers and video journalists in cities across France to document nationwide cost of living protests on Saturday.
Here is a round up of what they are witnessing as security forces seek to prevent a repeat of violence and looting that erupted on the sidelines of similar demonstrations last weekend.
‘Beating up a lot of people’
Police used tear gas and baton charged protesters at the end of the march at Porte de Vincennes on the eastern fringes of Paris.

“The police started moving towards everyone, telling them to get down and back off. They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters,” said a student, David, who was shaking and bleeding from a gash on his face.
“They were moving really fast and beating up a lot of people. The one of the police officers threw a baton at my face. There was blood everywhere.”
Residents peering out their apartment windows in one classic, Haussmann style building hurriedly slammed them shut and retreated after police fired tear gas near the front door.
‘It makes me sick’
In northern Lille, where the main march began in a calmer atmosphere than last week, protesters chanted “ACAB” — an English language acronym condemning police.

After an hour, the first tear gas canisters plunged part of the march into an opaque, stinging haze. A few projectiles were thrown at police. “We got gassed even though we weren’t doing anything,” said Eline, 23, her eyes full of tears. She said she was demonstrating for the first time.

Appoline, 25, admitted she was “terrified” to join the demonstration, having been shocked by images of police action circulating in recent days. She carried a sign that read: “For all those among us who have been maimed”, a reference to people hurt in recent protests.

“I hesitated to come,” said the psychology student. But “when I see young people losing eyes or hands, it makes me sick,” she whispered, as the Lille procession set off in the rain, accompanied by the beat of techno music.
‘Warzone’

Jeremy Costeweiss, a 21 year old medical student, told AFP he was attending the march in Paris as he feared “things are going to erupt” and he wanted to help people who may get tear gassed or hurt in confrontations.

First responder Alexandre B, speaking to AFP in Paris, described last week’s protests as a “warzone”. He said he had handled seven emergency interventions, including two cases of head trauma and two open fractures.
Saturday’s march was “nothing like” the week before, he added.
Umbrellas and hoods went up as the rain began to intensify over Paris.
‘Don’t do anything stupid’
Several thousand protesters began marching in pouring rain in Bordeaux.
Among them was an older CGT union activist who locked eyes with two masked youths in black tracksuits, and told them: “We’re not here to mess around — don’t do anything stupid.”
At the front of the march, police were nowhere to be seen. “No cops, no problems,” laughed another CGT union member.
Anger
Lucie, a 42 year old designer living in Begles, told AFP at a march in Bordeaux that the violence of last weekend was “unfortunate” but “a form of anger that one can understand”.

“The truth is, if you’ve never known what it’s like to go hungry, to struggle to make ends meet at the end of the month, or to have no idea what your future holds, you can’t truly grasp the kind of anger that can breed,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Protesters take shelter from a police water cannon near Porte de Vincennes during a nationwide demonstration over rising living costs and public services in Paris on October 24, 2026. — AFP pic
More tear gas
French police fired tear gas in Lyon, Lille, Marseille, Nantes and Toulouse as the protests went on.

Protesters could be seen running as tear gas canisters were launched in Nantes. Police also used a water cannon as they blocked access to a bridge crossing the Loire river, while some demonstrators hurled small projectiles in their direction.
One protester could be seen kicking back a tear gas canister during a demonstration in Toulouse, while another tried to do the same in Lyon.
‘Disappointed’
The only authorised march in Paris began at Porte d’Italie with thousands of people walking in a festive, calm atmosphere beneath cool, overcast skies.
Some carried placards with slogans such as “Macron in the corner” – referring to the French president – and “We expected nothing, yet we’re still disappointed”.

“We’re all here because we want to protest peacefully but people also need to understand that the anger is real. We’ve been walked all over for 10 years,” one protester in a Doctor Who hat who gave their name only as Aurore told AFP.
Ynyane, 19, was dressed as Dragon Ball anime hero Son Goku, a costume he chose “to give people hope”.
“Taxes are a bit too high and I have to support people who are struggling,” he added.
‘I’m also afraid’

High school students who gathered in Toulouse on Saturday spoke of their fears attending a demonstration, after weeks which have seen teenagers wounded and maimed in clashes between police and protesters.

Given the clashes last week and “the repression we faced – which was horrific – I think some people might not be keen on coming today”, 17 year old Ella, a student at the Lycee Marcelin Berthelot in Toulouse, told AFP.
“I’m also afraid of what might happen to me at a protest these days. But the truth is, we can’t give up. Even with this fear, we’re not giving up.”
‘Distressing’
At Porte de Vincennes, where the Paris march finished, some businesses had been barricaded, although many had their shutters down.

“It’s distressing. I don’t know where we’re heading,” said Dominique, an employee at a car rental company who preferred not to give her full name. “My grievance is with the rioters — those who come specifically to smash things and to steal.”
Police are ‘faster’
A 21 year old student protester in Lyon, where demonstrators were tear gassed on Saturday, said police were “highly mobile”.
“We keep moving around but since the police have vehicles, they’re faster. They manage to break up the groups before they can even really form,” he said.
“We end up exchanging information like criminals. We’re in small groups – sometimes just pairs – trying to share updates and find other people, but it’s extremely difficult.”
‘Still open’

Near Paris’s Bastille square, a clothing store removed all its merchandise ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up despite signs insisting it was “still open”. Many retailers in the capital had wooden boards covering windows.

A heavy police presence could be seen at Bastille, where police used a megaphone to tell the small crowd that the planned demonstration had been banned from the area, ordering protesters to go to the alternate route near Porte d’Italie “immediately”.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A protester lights a flare near Porte de Vincennes during a nationwide demonstration over rising living costs and public services in Paris on October 24, 2026. — AFP pic
Not ‘just one grievance’

“I don’t think the French people have just one grievance,” said Aliyah, 22, sitting with her mother Ludovine at a cafe terrace near the Old Port in Marseille as they waited for demonstrations. She said people’s primary concern was rising costs.

“The people are growing poorer, the people are unhappy, so they take to the streets to protest,” she said, adding that bans on the demonstrations in some cities “only makes us more determined to show up”.
‘Curiosity’
Shops and restaurants were open mid morning in Grenoble — although a curfew was in place in parts of the city and several shopping centres from 6pm.

Francois Xavier Chambron, who works at a bar on the city’s Grenette Square, said they planned to stay open at least for lunch, noting that they already had reservations and that people would be around “out of sheer curiosity”.
Demonstrators gathered for an authorised protest in the afternoon where one participant carried a sign reading: “And so freedom is extinguished under the rain of tear gas”.
‘Hotter than fascists’
Thousands of people yelling anti fascist slogans marched in the city of Orleans against a congress by the far right National Rally (RN) party of Marine Le Pen.
The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron.
“Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”.
Tear gas in Lyon
Police fired tear gas to disperse about 150 protesters in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations.
Police fired several tear gas grenades to clear a group gathered near a university building and the city police station. Police moved in as protesters tried to block a road.

Earlier a police helicopter could be seen flying over the city, with security forces patrolling and armoured vehicles and riot police vans parked nearby. Shops were boarded up, with private security guards in front of some. — AFP
0f2450d462dda48e: NAHAL OZ (Israel), Oct 25 — Danny Rahamim pauses for a few moments as he thinks about his neighbours here on an Israeli kibbutz just a few hundred metres from Gaza.
“I’m probably the most left-wing person here,” he said.

If that was true before October 7, 2023, when Hamas fighters stormed the border and carried out their unprecedented attack, it is even more true today, as Israel readies to vote in its first election since the country’s deadliest ever day.

With a sun-tanned bald head and sporting small glasses, Rahamim has spent 50 of his 72 years here at Nahal Oz, which, like many of Israel’s kibbutzim – small communities in the countryside where all work is shared – has historically reflected the socialist ethos of the country’s founders.
The kibbutzim were once bastions of the left, voting for peace with the Palestinians, but three years ago they found themselves on the frontlines of the Hamas attacks.

Sixteen of Nahal Oz’s 400 residents were killed. Thanks to the proximity of a military base, Rahamim explained, the death toll was significantly lower than at the neighbouring kibbutzim of Kfar Aza, where 64 people died, or Beeri, where 102 died.
“People changed their minds” after the attack, he said.
“Most of them didn’t turn right-wing. But they say they don’t believe anymore that things can get better with our neighbours,” said Rahamim, who serves as the kibbutz’s spokesman.
“I’m not giving up,” he said repeatedly under the flower-covered gazebo of his house.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Danny, a Nahal Oz resident, shows his sunflower tattoo bearing the Hebrew words ‘The Way to Hope’, commemorating the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, at the kibbutz near the Gaza border on October 22, 2026. — AFP pic
The peace camp has nearly vanished from Israeli politics.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the veteran right-winger whose long career is on the line in Tuesday’s election, has run his campaign on promises of preventing a Palestinian state. His chief opponent, centre-right former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has cast himself as being even more firmly opposed to it.
‘Killing the idea of a better future’
On the walls in Nahal Oz, the bullet holes have disappeared under a fresh coat of paint. But the memories remain ever-present. Rahamim said his own children tell him he is naive.
His grandson, who is almost four, rides his bicycle to the sound of birds chirping.
Above his yard, strewn with oranges that fell from trees, can be heard the constant buzzing of surveillance drones as Israel keeps an eye on the Gaza border.
“It looks quiet. But there were bodies everywhere,” said his stepdaughter, Naama Zadok-Rahamim.
The 37-year-old community employee wears a black T-shirt paying tribute to one of her slain neighbours and a Star of David around her neck. In her eyes, there is anger.
“What I expect from leaders is real security — someone who’s going to make sure that something like this doesn’t happen again,” she said.
During previous cycles of violence, when she heard the bombs falling on the other side of the border, she thought of the suffering of her “neighbours”.
“Now it’s hard for me to make the separation between Hamas and the other population. I don’t know if there’s much difference,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Israeli right-wing members of the Nachala settler organisation are seen at a newly built camp site at a field near the Israeli Kibbutz of Nahal Oz in southern Israel, by the Israel-Gaza border on October 22, 2026. — AFP pic
Nadav Perez, a 44-year-old hospital worker, has always voted for the left or the far left.
Before the attack, he was involved in a project to build a clinic for patients from Gaza. The regional council official behind the initiative was killed defending his kibbutz in Kfar Aza.
“I wondered if the terrorists who killed him knew that their bullets were killing the idea of a better future,” Perez said.
Since then, “my compassion is more blurred,” he admitted, his one-year-old son in his arms.
“I’m sorry to say it,” he said, “but I don’t really care what’s happening on the other side.”
He said he had not decided how to vote in Tuesday’s election. But he will not vote for Netanyahu, angry he has not taken responsibility for the failure to prevent the October 7 attack.
Ruins nearby

Danny Rahamim, for his part, will vote for the centre-left candidate Yair Golan, noting that he is the only major party leader who has made clear he would govern with lawmakers from Israel’s Arab minority.
Looking out on Gaza from an observation post, he pointed to the fences that were so easily breached on October 7.
What once were the first houses on the Gaza side, just 750 metres (820 yards) away, are now nothing but rubble. In the distance, Gaza City also lies in ruins and a burst of gunfire rings out.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Danny, a resident Kibbutz of Nahal Oz, points at the adjacent Gaza border, at the Israeli Kibbutz of Nahal Oz in southern Israel on October 22, 2026. — AFP pic
More than 10 years ago, his youngest daughter, then a teenager, had a panic attack during a bombing.
“‘If we can hear these bombs so strongly here, how can the children of Gaza stand it?’” he recalled her saying.
“I thought to myself that maybe I had done something right,” he said.
But she, too, has changed. She no longer speaks of the children on the other side, more than 21,500 of whom have been killed, according to Unicef, in the Israeli offensive since the October 7 attack.
According to her father, she is now convinced that Palestinians in Gaza are “all the same — all they wait for is to kill us”.
But even with the proximity to Gaza, she eventually decided to return to the kibbutz. “For children, it’s heaven,” Rahamim said. — AFP
9f4e4fe04afae328: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Palm oil blended in Malaysia must carry accurate declarations of origin, as any inaccuracy could undermine the integrity and reputation of Malaysian products in international markets, a maritime expert said.

Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) Faculty of Maritime Studies senior lecturer Dr Madzli Harun said that while palm oil blending was permitted in the industry, the process did not automatically make the finished product Malaysian in origin.

He said a product’s country of origin was determined under the applicable Rules of Origin (RoO), which take into account processing methods, raw material content and criteria set out under the relevant trade regulations.

“If the original bill of lading (B/L) states that the refined, bleached and deodorised (RBD) palm olein originates from Indonesia, subsequently blending the product in Malaysia does not automatically make it a Malaysian-origin product.

“The B/L may be amended after a vessel leaves the port of loading and while it is sailing to the port of destination, but such amendments must be supported by reasonable grounds and valid documentation,” he said.

Madzli said blending alone might not satisfy RoO requirements or change a product’s country of origin, and operators must therefore show that the processing carried out meets the relevant criteria before the finished product can be declared Malaysian in origin.
“In the Asean context, the Asean Trade in Goods Agreement (Atiga) sets out rules of origin that include criteria such as Regional Value Content (RVC), change in tariff classification and cumulation.

“The use of raw materials from Asean member states may be taken into account when determining the origin of a finished product under certain circumstances, subject to the requirements of the agreement.

“Operators cannot simply blend oil from Indonesia with Malaysian oil and then label it ‘Made in Malaysia’. The finished product must meet the prescribed requirements before it can qualify for recognition as Malaysian-origin,” he said.

He said the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD), the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) and the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) should examine the relevant documentation within their respective jurisdictions to ensure blending activities and origin declarations complied with the applicable regulations.
“The documents that need to be examined include import and export records, certificates of origin, the quantity of imported oil, the volume of Malaysian oil used and records of the blending process.
“Traceability is also important to ensure that the origin of raw materials can be identified even after products from different countries have been blended.

“Even if the finished product qualifies for Malaysian-origin status under the applicable rules, records of raw materials imported from Indonesia must still be retained. Information on the origin of those materials must not simply be erased after blending,” he said.

He also warned that if a blended product was found to be contaminated, Malaysia could suffer reputational damage, face cargo rejections by buyers and potentially encounter legal action, depending on the circumstances and the parties responsible.
Madzli said false declarations could also lead to action under the relevant laws, including Section 133 of the Customs Act 1967, if the elements of an offence under the provision were established.

Meanwhile, maritime expert Prof Nazery Khalid said documentation for blended cargoes should accurately reflect the composition and characteristics of the resulting product to avoid doubts about its contents.

He said this was important because if a blended cargo was found to be contaminated and posed a health risk to consumers after export, Malaysia could suffer reputational damage if the product was perceived to have originated from the country.
“The recent food poisoning incident in Taiwan involving contaminated cooking oil should serve as a lesson.

“As one of the world’s major palm oil producers, Malaysia must ensure that its exported oil meets quality and integrity standards, while ensuring that its processing, documentation and shipment are carried out properly,” he said.

f0a3908729965b0b: LONDON: UK leader Andy Burnham indicated he was open to readopting the EU's free movement rules as part of Britain's future relationship with the bloc, said a report published Sunday.
The Labour prime minister has promised to lay out different options for closer relations with Europe around the time of a long-awaited UK-EU summit in Brussels next month.

Burnham, who has even touted the possibility of Britain applying to rejoin the EU one day, said the country should have an "honest discussion" about how immigration to the UK has changed since Brexit.
Immigration was one of the main reasons for Britons voting narrowly to leave the EU during the divisive 2016 referendum that was triggered by the right-wing Conservatives.
Burnham said immigration into Britain had been "different" since the country left the EU in early 2020.
"It was a type of immigration that perhaps wasn't as difficult (as now)," he told the Sunday Times newspaper.
"Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different.
"The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we've just got to have an honest discussion about those things," he said.
Burnham, in office since July, has committed to predecessor Keir Starmer's 2024 election-winning manifesto, which ruled out the return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.
That means he may seek to win a mandate for any major change in Britain's relationship with the EU at the next general election, which is currently not expected until 2029.
Burnham told the Sunday Times he "can't see myself ever recommending anything that would involve joining" the euro or the Schengen borderless area, which the UK was not a part of pre-Brexit.
Nigel Farage, leader of the anti-immigrant Reform UK party, called Burnham's comments on free movement a "total betrayal of Brexit Britain".
Burnham and EU leaders are hopeful of striking deals on food and drink, youth mobility and emissions tradings when they meet on Nov 20.

ee9206c266412548: PARIS: Rescuers were searching on Sunday for five people missing after an oil rig sank off the coast of Gabon, the operating company said.

"At the time of the incident, there were 115 personnel onboard the rig," the Bermuda-headquartered firm said in a statement.

ee0987732ffe7eed: KOTA BHARU, Oct 25 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has predicted that Pakatan Harapan will lose power in Putrajaya at the 16th general election, according to online reports.

644501d189d9f4ff: PETALING JAYA: Tiada ikan piranha ditemukan atau ditangkap sepanjang program mitigasi ikan asing di Empangan Klau di Raub, Pahang yang berlangsung selama dua hari bermula semalam.
Bagaimanapun, Ketua Pengarah Perikanan Adnan Hussain berkata keadaan itu tidak boleh ditafsirkan sebagai bukti bahawa spesies berkenaan tiada di empangan berkenaan.

Katanya, sebelum ini penemuan ikan piranha telah disahkan di kawasan tersebut dan program mitigasi ini adalah antara usaha bagi mengawal populasi ikan asing serta mengurangkan risiko gangguan terhadap spesies ikan tempatan.

“Tiada ikan piranha ditemukan atau ditangkap sepanjang program ini. Namun, pemantauan dan penilaian saintifik perlu diteruskan bagi mengenal pasti kehadiran serta taburan spesies berkenaan,” katanya dalam kenyataan lapor Bernama.
Sebelum ini, tular dalam media sosial mengenai penemuan seekor ikan yang didakwa menyerupai jenis piranha di Empangan Klau sehingga menimbulkan pelbagai reaksi masyarakat.

Jabatan itu dalam kenyataan sama memaklumkan selain aktiviti tangkapan, penyelidikan menggunakan kaedah DNA persekitaran (environmental DNA atau eDNA) turut dilaksanakan dalam program ini bagi membantu mengesan kemungkinan kehadiran ikan piranha di Empangan Klau.
Kaedah ini membolehkan sampel air dianalisis bagi mengesan bahan genetik yang mungkin ditinggalkan oleh organisma akuatik.
“Keputusan akhir penyelidikan eDNA akan ditentukan selepas proses analisis dan penilaian saintifik selesai.
"Sebarang kesimpulan mengenai status kehadiran piranha di Empangan Klau perlu mengambil kira hasil analisis tersebut bersama maklumat pemantauan dan bukti lapangan yang berkaitan,” katanya.
Program mitagasi yang dijalankan di empangan berkeluasan kira-kira 25km persegi itu melibatkan 150 peserta, terdiri daripada 100 pemancing, 32 peserta menjala dan 18 peserta menjaring.
Sepanjang program, sebanyak 156.6kg ikan asing direkodkan, melibatkan tiga kumpulan utama, iaitu Peacock Bass, Tilapia Zebra dan Lampam Jawa.

ab2f533173b2410a: NINGBO: World number one Elena Rybakina won her fourth title of an outstanding season with a ruthless straight-sets victory over Leylah Fernandez in the Ningbo Open final on Sunday.
The top seed and defending champion cruised to a 6-2, 6-2 win in 73 minutes over the world number 30 from Canada.
Rybakina, the Australian and US Open champion, collected her 15th WTA crown in all and went a long way towards securing the year-end number-one ranking.
"Thank you all you guys for an amazing atmosphere," the Moscow-born Kazakh said in her victory speech to the crowd.
"Every day it's amazing to play in front of you. It gives a lot of motivation and energy to keep on going.
"A second win here, it's such a special place for me," she said.
Rybakina broke and then held her own serve with a delicious two-handed crosscourt backhand for a 4-2 lead in the opening set.
She immediately put Fernandez under pressure again on the Canadian's serve and it was soon 5-2 to the reigning champion when her opponent fired into the net.
The 27-year-old Rybakina, who missed this month's Wuhan Open with a foot injury, began to turn the screw and sealed the set to love in under 40 minutes.
Fernandez, who was looking to win her second title in as many months, was broken once more as a clinical Rybakina grabbed a 2-1 second-set lead.
Rybakina saw off two break points in the fourth game to hold, and with that, Fernandez's resistance was broken.
Rybakina was within sight of retaining her trophy after breaking once more for 5-2, then sealed the deal on her first championship point with a searing forehand.
9c43fb825ff142a7: TEHRAN, Oct 25 — Iran’s parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Sunday called for a campaign to cut gas consumption by at least 10 per cent, with officials anticipating shortages as winter approaches.

While a major producer, Iran has long suffered shortages of natural gas, essential for powering heating systems, which have been exacerbated by war with the United States and Israel that began in February.
During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the two countries struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran.
Winter in Iran often sees temperatures drop below freezing, especially in the country’s north.
“To get through the approaching winter, a nationwide effort is essential ... to reduce gas consumption by at least 10 per cent,” said Ghalibaf in a video carried by Iranian media.

“Anyone who saves gas, regardless of the amount, will immediately receive the corresponding proceeds in their bank account, allowing everyone to see the tangible impact of those savings on their household budget.”

Earlier in October, First Vice-President Mohammad Reza Aref said the government anticipated a daily “gas shortfall of 100 million to 250 million cubic metres during the cold season because of the damage caused by the war,” according to the official IRNA news agency.
He added that he hoped to restore the supply of around 100 million cubic metres by the start of winter.

An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control over the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel.
Iran has claimed control over the strait since the outbreak of the war and has regularly targeted vessels that attempt crossings without its authorisation.

In response, Washington has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and in August announced what it called an “economic asphyxiation” campaign on Iran aimed at strangling its already battered economy. — AFP
